Is A24 Finally Big Enough to Be Considered a Major Studio?
articles.content: Earlier this year when IndieWire reported that A24 had settled a dispute with Marcus Theaters over theatrical terms, a back and forth that kept some of A24 ‘s summer titles like “The Invite,” “Tony,” and “Onslaught” out of the fourth-largest chain in the country, the reason was because of a debate over A24’s size. When you have blockbusters as big as “Backrooms” and “Marty Supreme,” why would you still want theatrical terms that lump you in with the specialized, little guys? This is the question that Hollywood — and even perhaps A24 internally — should start asking: Should A24 now be considered a major studio? Not merely a restructuring of departments over the coming years or a revamping of its centerpiece offering, the four-decades-old Spirit Awards , but something more expansive, place-based, and integrated. articles.content: EXCLUSIVE: The Project Hail Mary star and AT&T spokeswoman, Milana Vayntrub , is boarding Tate Taylor’s marriage counselor thriller which we first told you about, Cupid . The psychological thriller, written by the Van Dyke Brothers ( Don’t Worry Darling ), is in production in Natchez, Mississippi. The pic is produced by Wyolah Films. Cupid follows a couple (Ridley and Criss) whose relationship is on the rocks as they try, over one weekend, to repair their marriage at the home of a seemingly helpful but unorthodox marriage counselor (Zeta-Jones). What starts out as a hopeful endeavor quickly turns dark as her methods become crueler and more dangerous. Vayntrub’s credits also include Netflix’s Monsters: The Erik and Lyle Menendez Story , in which she portrayed prosecutor Pam Bozanich, and Bad Shabbos , which debuted at the 2024 Tribeca Film Festival. She also directed and starred in the short film Pickled Herring and previously appeared in Werewolves Within , Die Hart , This Is Us and Silicon Valley . The actress is repped by Innovative Artists Entertainment and Artists First. articles.title: Bassam Tariq On Exiting Marvel’s ‘Blade’: “Life’s Too Short To Make Sh** Films”
articles.content: Bassam Tariq was once attached to direct Marvel’s Blade with Mahershala Ali , but eventually exited the project. In a new interview, the Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother director reveals why he decided not to helm the superhero movie. “Life’s too short to make shit films, so that was my big lesson: I have to have full control over my script,” Tariq told The New Arab . “If we disagree, it’s between them and me. articles.title: E.J. Carroll Dies: ‘The Deuce,’ ‘Boardwalk Empire,’ ‘Law & Order’ Actor Was 66
articles.content: E.J. Carroll , a veteran character actor whose credits include The Deuce , Boardwalk Empire , Blue Bloods three Law & Order series and Grand Theft Auto V , died November 19. He was 66. His rep Jon Mason of Mason-Lewis Entertainment said Carroll died suddenly while en route to a voice-over booking, but he did not provide a cause of death. Born on May 21, 1960, Carroll appeared in features, television, short films and video games during a nearly three-decade screen career. His first screen credit was playing a cop in a 1998 episode of NBC’s Law & Order, and he would appear as other characters in three other episodes through 2004. He also had roles in two early-2000s episodes of its juggernaut spinoff Law & Order: SVU and two more in Law & Order: Criminal Intent that decade. He would appear in a number of movies during the later 2000s and into the 2010s including Darren Aronfsky’s acclaimed 2009 drama The Wrestler, along with The Cake Eaters, The Capers, The Winning Season, The Hungry Ghosts, A Fish Story and the Robert De Niro-Kate Beckinsale pic Everything’s Fine, among others. Carroll played Sheriff Victor Sickles in two 2012 episodes of HBO’s lauded period crime drama Boardwalk Empire, from Tenrence Winter and MArtin Scorsese and starring Steve Buscemi, appeared in episode of FX’s Glenn Close-Rose Byrne legal thriller Damages that same year. He went on to guest on NBC’s The Blacklist, CBS’ Blue Bloods, HBO’s High Maintenance , FX’s Pose and Netflix’s Marvel series The Punisher. He landed perhaps his most recognizable role in 2017, recurring on the HBO’ ‘s The Deuce as Fat Mooney, who ran a New York City sex shop owned by Frankie Martino (James Franco). He appeared in a half-dozen episodes of the series about the rise of the porn industry in the 1970s and ’80s. Most recently, Carroll filmed a role in A Delicate Arrangement , the upcoming film written and produced by Jayce Bartok and directed by Nick Sandow. articles.title: Steven Paul Talks Up Federal Film & TV Tax Credit: “It’s Going To Be Good For The World” – Industry Days Doha
articles.content: Hollywood veteran Steven Paul carried a flag for the push for a Hollywood film and TV incentive to Qatar on Friday. Speaking in a fireside chat at the Qatar Film Committee ’s Industry Days event in Doha, Paul said the proposed tax credit, covering between 20 to 30% of the U.S. spend, would be good for the world, without explaining the reasoning behind this declaration. “I’ve got two tiers to discuss, regarding why it’ll be good for the world, but right away, it’s going to be good for the entertainment business because a lot more money comes into the business, which makes it more healthy,” he said. articles.title: E.J. Carroll, ‘Law & Order,’ ‘GTA 5’ and ‘Blue Bloods’ Actor, Dies at 66
articles.content: E.J. Carroll, who appeared in projects including “ The Deuce ,” “Law & Order” and “Grand Theft Auto V,” died on Thursday. He was 66. Carroll died suddenly Thursday morning, his rep confirmed to Variety . No cause of death has been provided. Throughout his nearly 30-year career, Carroll’s credits included Darren Aronfsky’s “The Wrestler” and Robert De Niro and Kate Beckinsale’s “Everybody’s Fine,” as well as “The Cake Eaters,” “The Capers,” “The Winning Season,” “The Hungry Ghosts” and “A Fish Story.” One of the actor’s most recognizable roles was as Fat Mooney in HBO’s “The Deuce,” where his character ran a sex shop owned by Frankie Martino (James Franco). Related Stories Cannes Condemns Five-Year Prison Sentence Against Iranian Palme d’Or Winner Jafar Panahi and Pleads for International Support Born on May 21, 1960, Carroll made his on-screen debut in 1998 as a police officer in “Law & Order,” later returning for two episodes of “Law & Order: SVU” and an additional two in “Law & Order: Criminal Intent.” As a guest star, Carroll appeared in projects such as “The Blacklist,” “Blue Bloods,” “High Maintenance,” “Pose” and “The Punisher.” He also starred as Sheriff Victor Sickles in two episodes of Terence Winter and Martin Scorsese’s “Boardwalk Empire” in 2012 before going on to appear in an episode of “Damages,” which starred Glenn Close and Rose Byrne, that same year. He also voiced a character in “Grand Theft Auto V” in 2013 and played Dr. Scott in the concert version of “The Rocky Horror Show,” titled “The Rocky Horror Tribute Show.” The concert ran for one night in 2007 to raise money for cancer charities Acting for a Cure and Komen for the Cure. Prior to his death, Carroll most recently starred in “A Delicate Arrangement,” the upcoming Vivian Leigh biopic. Starring Carla Gugino as the “Gone With the Wind” actress, the film is written and produced by Jayce Bartok and directed by Nick Sandow.

articles.title: ‘I Play Rocky’ Fact vs Fiction: Butkus the Dog, Bloody Knuckles and Stallone’s Fight to Get ‘Rocky’ Made
articles.content: The beloved classic “ Rocky ” premiered half a century ago this week. Five decades later, “ I Play Rocky ,” in theaters now, tells the story of how unknown writer and actor Sylvester Stallone shoulders his way into not just writing the script but playing the iconic lead role of boxer Rocky Balboa, culminating in a best picture Oscar. In the year 2026, is it really possible to go back in time and depict the making of “Rocky” with perfect accuracy? The unvarnished truth doesn’t always make for the best dramatic impact in a movie — and Stallone and the filmmaking team have told somewhat varying stories over the past 50 years. articles.title: CMA Awards See a 55% Ratings Bump in Key Adult Demo With Taylor Swift’s Return to the Show
articles.content: The CMA Awards ‘ producers knew it; they knew her. What they undoubtedly knew was that a performance by Taylor Swift would bring a ratings bonanza to the 60th annual telecast, with the only question being how big a boost. It was a substantial one, as ratings released Friday showed the 2026 show being up 26% in total viewers and an even more impressive 55% gain in the key 18-49 demo, versus the previous year’s tallies. With help from Swift’s performance of a “I Knew It, I Knew You”/”Our Song” medley, the CMAs had their highest overall viewership in seven years, ABC announced. The show drew 7.62 total viewers, versus 6.03 million in 2025, for that 26% increase. The 18-49 share of the audience, where the 55% growth was found, had the telecast earning a 1.01 rating, compared to a 0.65 share last year. America has certainly been high on Ella Langley , who did at least as well as anticipated in the awards, sweeping nearly every category she was up for to win a record six CMA Awards. articles.content: For costume designers Janie Bryant and John Glaser, outfitting a character is another form of storytelling. “When an actor appears on screen, you see the costume before they even say a word,” says Bryant, an Emmy winner whose credits include “Mad Men,” “Deadwood” and Taylor Sheridan shows including “Dutton Ranch” and other “Yellowstone” spinoffs. “That’s the magic of costume design.” Related Stories Cannes Condemns Five-Year Prison Sentence Against Iranian Palme d’Or Winner Jafar Panahi and Pleads for International Support Bryant and Glaser, an Emmy winner who has worked on “Bridgerton,” “Gotham” and “Harry Potter 20th Anniversary: Return to Hogwarts,” joined Variety’s senior film reporter Rebecca Rubin in partnership with the Round Top Film Festival for a panel titled, “Who, What, Wear: The Importance of Costume in Storytelling.” “It’s kind of our bible,” Bryant said. “We can see the period. We can read how these characters are speaking to one another, the mood, the feeling. The script is everything.” Once they have a sense of the characters, they can start to build out their looks. That involves extensive research, especially if they are curating a wardrobe from decades (or centuries) ago, rather than a modern story. articles.content: Twelve people were killed and 6,000 structures were destroyed in the January 2025 fire A jury on Friday found a man guilty for starting the deadly January 2025 Palisades Fire that killed 12 people and destroyed 6,000 home and structures. Jonathan Rinderknecht was convicted on two federal counts: destruction of property by means of fire, and arson affecting property used in interstate commerce. Prosecutors used surveillance camera footage of Rinderknecht driving through the Pacific Palisades region prior to the fire to build their case. They also argued that DNA from a green BIC barbeque lighter matched his DNA. Friday’s conviction comes after Rinderknecht’s first federal trial was declared a mistrial five months prior. Back in June, a jury informed U.S. District Judge Anne Hwang that it was deadlocked on all three felony counts against Rinderknecht with 10 jurors favoring acquittal, according to media reports. His retrial began with jury selection on Nov. 2. A verdict was reached 18 days later. “We respect the jury’s work and the long, difficult process that brought us to today’s verdict,” LAFD wrote in a statement. “Our first thought remains with the families of those we lost and for everyone in our community whose lives were changed by this fire,” the statement continued. “No verdict, however important, could ever undo that loss.” “Because the criminal sentencing and related civil matters remain pending, we will not comment further at this time.” Rinderknecht will be sentenced on March 17, 2027. The 30-year-old former Uber driver faces a minimum of 5 years and a maximum of 40 years in prison, according to prosecutors.

articles.content: The veteran character performer died suddenly on the way to a voice over session Thursday Veteran character and voice over actor E.J. Carroll died suddenly Thursday on the way to a voice over recording session. The actor was 66. His manager Jon Mason confirmed his death to TheWrap. The case of death has not been determined. The actor was best known for his roles in “The Deuce,” “Law & Order” and “Boardwalk Empire.” He most recently appeared in “The Mayflower” as a stalker. Carroll was born in 1960, and throughout his acting career appeared in films, television and video games. His first credit was for playing a cop in a 1998 episode of “Law & Order.” He appeared in the series across three other episodes through 2004. He also appeared in spinoff series for the legal drama “Law & Order: SVU” and “Law & Order: Criminal Intent.” The actor went on to appear in several films in the 2000s and 2010s, including “The Night Listener,” Darren Aronfsky’s “The Wrestler” and Robert De Niro and Kate Beckinsale-led “Everybody’s Fine.” One of his most recognizable role was his recurring role in HBO’s “The Deuce” as Fat Mooney, who ran a New York City sex shop owned by Frankie Martino (James Franco). He acted in six episodes of the drama series. In the video game sector, Carroll voiced a character in Grand Theft Auto V and Need for Speed: Undercover. Other notable television credits included “Blue Bloods,” “The Blacklist,” “The Punisher” and “Pose.” His loved ones will host a Celebration of Life service in the new year in New York City.

articles.title: ‘Disclosure Day’ Did Its Biggest Stunts Practically, So the VFX Team Worked Hard to Look Invisible — Watch
articles.summary: At IndieWire's Craft Roundtables, "Disclosure Day" VFX supervisor Matthew Butler explained how stunt work and effects can combine to make movie magic.
articles.content: Even six decades into his Hollywood career, Steven Spielberg is still synonymous with a brand of movie magic and spectacle that very few can rival. And when he decides to direct a new popcorn blockbuster like “ Disclosure Day ,” you know you’re in for a few dazzling sequences. One of the most exciting moments in the film comes when a train collides into a car with stars Josh O’Connor and Emily Blunt close at hand. The sequence tested every department, from camera and production design to visual effects. And during IndieWire’s recent Craft Roundtables, VFX Supervisor Matthew Butler explained the unique challenge of incorporating subtle VFX work into a scene where so much happens in camera. Related Stories How World-Class Filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev Came Back to Life for ‘Minotaur’ How a Filipino Facial Expression in ‘Forgotten Island’ Became a Universal Symbol of Representation “With Steven, he wants everything to be as practical as it can be,” Butler said. “We had a real train. A real train, a real car attached to that train, it was being dragged on a real track. That actually did happen.” But while Spielberg’s preferences were clear, Butler clarified that blockbusters on this scale rarely come down to a binary choice between practical effects and VFX. The biggest scenes often contain elements of both, as the pairing between in-camera human acting and cutting edge post-production is what leads to movie magic. “When you combine some of the live action blue screen work, clearly that’s your lead actor and actress there, and your stunt work where it’s like ‘Oh my God, that looks really real’ and the stuff that you just can’t do that’s just too dangerous … that’s where visual effects came in,” he said. “But I wouldn’t say it was a visual effects sequence. It was a sequence that contained all of those, and it came together in the right way.” More coverage from IndieWire’s Craft Roundtables will be published here over the coming weeks. articles.title: How a Filipino Facial Expression in ‘Forgotten Island’ Became a Universal Symbol of Representation
articles.summary: Directors Joel Crawford and Januel Mercado told IndieWire about crafting the Filipino mythology-inspired animated movie and why lip pointing is iconic.
articles.content: As soon as the first clips from DreamWorks’ latest animated film , “ Forgotten Island ,” started popping up online, there was one specific shot that caught on fire online — the lip pointing. It happens at a goodbye party for Raissa Molina (Liza Soberano), who is heading to Caltech. Her best friend Jo (H.E.R.) is late to the party and asks around to see where Raissa is, when an older woman points with her lips in the right direction. It’s a small moment, a visual gag that can easily go over the audience’s heads amidst all the other jokes in the sequence. But audiences familiar with Filipino culture immediately caught on to it, as did Latino fans and many others who recognize that gesture as the most potent and accurate way to point at something. And in adding that specificity about the culture, it ends up being the most universal aspect of the movie because it invites everyone in.” The lip pointing may not happen in a pivotal scene, or be important for a character, but it became a sort of symbol for the film’s approach to representation. articles.title: Box Office: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Scores $21 Million in Previews, Second-Best Result of 2026
articles.summary: Who cares about "Grand Theft Auto 6"? The return to Panem is expected to earn more than $100 million.
articles.content: ““ The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping ” earned $21 million in Thursday previews and early screenings on Wednesday and is expected to dominate the box office this weekend. Analysts believe it will earn north of $100 million. The preview figures are the second-best of 2026, behind “Spider-Man: Brand New Day’s” massive $72 million haul. It’s also the second-best for the “Hunger Games” franchise, just behind the $25.5 million that “Catching Fire” earned in 2013. It’s a big improvement on the last “Hunger Games” prequel, “The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes,” which made $5.75 million in previews and kicked off with $44 million. That film would gross over $166 million domestically and nearly $364 million globally, figures that “Sunrise on the Reaping” is on pace to easily eclipse. “Sunrise on the Reaping” is based on Suzanne Collins’ bestselling novel of the same name. It tells the origin story of Haymitch Abernathy, the alcoholic former Hunger Games victor played by Woody Harrelson in the films. The sequel checks in with him at 16 as he’s forced to compete in gladiatorial combat. “East of Eden” breakout Joseph Zada plays Haymitch. He’s surrounded by an all-star cast that includes Jesse Plemons, Ralph Fiennes, Glenn Close, Kieran Culkin, Elle Fanning, Mckenna Grace, and Maya Hawke. Francis Lawrence, who helmed most of the series’ films, returns as director. Lionsgate, which is having a strong year at the box office thanks to “Michael,” is backing the “Hunger Games” sequel as it has the previous films. The biggest competition for “Sunrise on the Reaping” this weekend isn’t another major movie, but the release of “Grand Theft Auto 6,” which is expected to be a phenomenon. articles.summary: Beth de Araújo's sophomore outing, following her remarkable 2022 debut, is another finely-tuned exploration of the pervasive power and perversion of real evil.
articles.content: [Editor’s note: This review was originally published on January 23, 2026 during the 2026 Sundance Film Festival. Sumerian Pictures will release the film in limited theaters on Friday, November 20, with a wide release to follow on Friday, December 4.] At this point, filmmaker Beth de Araújo is two for two. Not just in terms of the quality of her films — impeccably crafted fever dreams of very different stripes and horrifyingly similar themes — but in how these films make the viewer feel. More concisely: with her “Soft & Quiet” and “ Josephine ,” de Araújo remains undefeated when it comes to making stunning films that I will both heartily recommend and never, ever watch again. articles.title: Walter Hill on Sam Peckinpah, Steve McQueen, and His Revolutionary Screenplay for ‘The Getaway’
articles.summary: The veteran screenwriter reflected on his first big hit in front of a packed crowd at the Academy Museum.
articles.content: In 1972, Walter Hill was a young screenwriter with just one produced movie (“Hickey & Boggs”) behind him when he scored an enviable gig: adapting Jim Thompson’s tough-as-nails crime novel “ The Getaway ” for actor/producer Steve McQueen (then one of the biggest movie stars in the world) and director Sam Peckinpah (then, as now, one of the greatest directors who ever lived). articles.summary: IndieWire debuts the premiere of an Oscar-eligible short from Zane Pais.
articles.content: A smoke break at the Signature Theatre ultimately resulted in one of Lois Smith ‘s most fascinating performances. The Tony Award winner met Zane Pais while they were both grabbing a quick cigarette while rehearsing plays. Pais had been an admirer of Smith’s work in stage productions like “The Inheritance” and films such as “Marjorie Prime” and “Five Easy Pieces,” and longed to collaborate. “She has the most amazing delivery of lines; she’s always able to do something so unexpected with the language,” Pais said during a recent Zoom interview with Smith. “I’ve seen Lois my whole life in so many amazing shows, just be so unbelievably present on stage and be such a generous actor, and just give these heartfelt and unexpected performances. I’m a big fucking fan.” Related Stories Is A24 Finally Big Enough to Be Considered a Major Studio? Bill Hader’s Feature Directorial Debut ‘They Know’ Lands at Black Bear So Pais wrote a short film , “Lightning Bug,” with Smith in mind. In it, she plays Lydia, a fiercely independent nonagenarian who is being pressured into selling the family home by her son and granddaughter. But things take an unexpected turn when a strange young man crashes their dinner, giving Lydia a chance to demonstrate she hasn’t missed a step despite her advanced age. “It was all there in the script,” Smith, who recently turned 96, said. “It wasn’t complex for me to pull it off even though the script is complex.” The role did require Smith to perform some fight choreography, but she seemed more nervous about singing a song on screen. “I really worried: Am I going to be able to do this?” Smith said. “They made me a tape, and I listened to it and listened to it and practiced.
